title: Clarinet Trio in D minor, Op. 3
notes: Three movements: Allegro ma non troppo, Andante, Allegro; early trio
rejectNote: The 'Clarinet Trio in D minor, Op. 3' on the Brilliant disc is Zemlinsky's (Op. 3, 1896, D minor, 3 movements, already in the catalogue as 104089); Fruehling's clarinet trio is Op. 40 in A minor (104921)

title: String Quartet No. 2
notes: Quatuor brillant with a showy first violin; three movements
rejectNote: The only recording cited (Quatuor Debussy, 'Onslow, Dancla, Rode') has Dancla's quartet as No. 8 in G, Op. 87; the 'Quatuor brillant No. 2' track is Rode's (IMSLP, Rode Op.Posth.2). No recording or edition of a Dancla No. 2 found. Candidate to add instead: Dancla String Quartet No. 8 in G major, Op. 87 (about 23 min)

title: Grand trio concertant in C minor, Op. 36
rejectNote: The Grand trio concertant in C minor, Op. 36 on Toccata TOCC 0417 (Trio Klengel) is by August Alexander Klengel (1783-1852), not the cellist Julius; Wikipedia lists it in his discography and IMSLP has it under him. Same work as 104940, with the same key, opus and four movements

title: Concert Waltz, Op. 13
notes: For four cellos; not on IMSLP
rejectNote: The only recording found (Naxos 8.574301, '48 Strings', track 18, 7:02) is of Wilhelm Fitzenhagen's Concert-Walzer for four cellos (Op. 31 per IMSLP and Radio Times; the Apple track says Op. 13). Julius Klengel's published list has no concert waltz; his Hymnus Op. 57 is the only Klengel work on that disc

title: Piano Trio, Op. 16
notes: Piano trio; years from the recording's track titles
rejectNote: Etcetera KTC1730 credits the Piano Trio Op. 16 (1882) to Joseph Callaerts, not Ryelandt; Presto lists 'Callaerts: Piano Trio, Op. 16'. Wikipedia gives Ryelandt two piano trios (Op. 57, Op. 131). Callaerts's trio could be its own entry if he passes the track-record rule.

title: Cardiac Arrest
notes: Based on a song by Madness; seven players with the piano part for four hands
rejectNote: Faber lists composers 'Thomas Adès, Madness' with 'Arranger: arranged by Thomas Adès' (premiere Composers Ensemble, 1995): an arrangement of Madness's song, not Adès's own music. Recorded (Warner, 2:39)

title: The History of Red
notes: For mezzo-soprano, piano, violin and cello; recorded live by ROCO
rejectNote: Composer's site: the work is for soprano and chamber orchestra; the piano-trio version was arranged by soprano Karen Hogle Brown from Esmail's piano reduction and score; the ROCO recording (20:28) is the chamber-orchestra version. Voice is soprano, not mezzo (Wikipedia's 'mezzo, piano, violin, cello' is wrong)
